I'm hiring one undergraduate research assistant to work with me on a
philosophy of science project. The project is called "[The Productive Role of
Error in AI-Driven Modeling](about.qmd)" and is funded by the Alfred P. Sloan
Foundation. If this sounds interesting to you, please read on and consider
applying. Feel free to email me if you have questions
(<span class="email-obfuscate" data-user="ryan.oloughlin" data-domain="qc.cuny.edu">ryan.oloughlin [at] qc.cuny.edu</span>).

## Background

Can getting things wrong be part of how science gets things right?
Philosophers of science have long asked how science manages to be reliable
when its individual models, theories, and practitioners are fallible. My new
research project takes up a version of this question in one of the most
consequential areas of science today: climate modeling, where scientists are
increasingly turning to AI. The project focuses on three questions. First, how
can scientists understand what an AI model is doing, and explain why it goes
wrong when it does? Second, can errors actually make scientific models
stronger over time, so that a model improves *because* it was pushed until it
broke? And third, how does the way scientists find, handle, and communicate
errors shape whether the rest of us should trust their results?

## The position

- **Paid:** a $3,500 stipend, funded by a Queens College Research Enhancement
  Grant
- **Time:** January 15 through May 15, 2027, at about 10 hours per week
  (roughly 175 hours in total). The schedule is flexible. The position may be
  extended if additional funding becomes available (which is my hope).
- **What you'll do:** read and summarize research in philosophy of science and
  philosophy of AI, write short literature review memos, meet with me regularly
  to discuss the readings and the project's open questions, and help prepare
  materials for the project's [workshop](workshop.qmd) at Queens College.

## What I'm looking for

This is meant to be a genuine research apprenticeship, not only a list of
assigned tasks. Our working sessions are a central part of the job. I'm
looking for someone who reads carefully, asks good questions, and is willing
to push back on my arguments when they think I've gotten something wrong.

Some familiarity with philosophy of science is helpful but not required. If
you're new to the field, we'll spend the first weeks of the position working
through some foundational readings together. No background in climate science
or AI is needed, and you don't need prior research experience.

The position is open to all Queens College undergraduates. Philosophy majors,
students in the BA/MA program, and students in the School of Earth and
Environmental Sciences are especially encouraged to apply.

## How to apply

Email the following to
<span class="email-obfuscate" data-user="ryan.oloughlin" data-domain="qc.cuny.edu">ryan.oloughlin [at] qc.cuny.edu</span>
with "RA Application" in the subject line:

1. A statement (one page, single-spaced, maximum) explaining why you're
   interested in the position, how it connects to your academic or
   professional plans, and what background you'd bring, whether in
   philosophy, science, or elsewhere
2. A resume
3. Optional: a writing sample, such as a paper from any course

Please do not use AI to write your statement or writing sample.

Applications are due **Tuesday, December 1, 2026**. I'll invite shortlisted
applicants to a short interview.
